nodes.name: Precursor Mixing and High-Temperature Shock
nodes.procedure: First, accurately weigh 4.0 mg of Pt(acac)2, 3.05 mg of Pd(acac)2, 2.95 mg of Ni(acac)2, 2H2O, 4.05 mg of Ru(acac)3, and 4.95 mg of Ir(acac)3, along with 5.0 mg of Vulcan XC-72R carbon black, and disperse them in 10 mL of acetone. Then, stir the mixture at 50 °C until the acetone completely evaporates, and grind the remaining solid into a uniform powder. Subsequently, spread the ground powder uniformly on a 5 cm × 2 cm carbon paper, and connect both ends of the carbon paper to the electrodes of HTS equipment. Perform a high-temperature pulse treatment at 600 °C in a tube furnace or other suitable reactor under an argon atmosphere.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) (Figure 5h) demonstrates lower charge-transfer resistance for PtPdIrNiCu/C.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) measurement (Figure 5i) derived from cyclic voltammetry ... yields an electrochemically active surface area of 36.2 mFcm-2.

nodes.evidence_snippet: atomic ratios of Pt, Ni, Ir, Pd, and Cu in PtNiIrPdCu/C measured by ICP-MS ... dissolution of Ni increased only slightly to 6.876 µg L-1.
